name: Shibaura Institute of Technology (SIT)
overview:
Shibaura Institute of Technology (SIT) has firmly maintained “learning through practice” as the philosophy in education of engineers ever since Tokyo Higher School of Industry and Commerce, the predecessor to SIT, was established in 1927. In response to the recent progress in the globalization of the economy, SIT is providing an up-to-date framework for “learning through practice” including intensive English Language programs, Project Based Learning programs under multicultural environment, along with many Hands-on subjects that has been preserved through SIT’s 91 years of history.

The initiative for educational reforms are supported by Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology and implemented in collaboration with other technical universities both in Japan and other countries, Japanese industries, and local communities in Tokyo and Saitama where our campuses are located.

SIT now aims to foster scientists and engineers who can contribute to the sustainable growth of the world by exposing our students to culturally diverse environments where they learn to cope with, collaborate with, and have ever-lasting friendships with fellow students from around the world.
administrative:
1. Application Dossier

You will be working directly with the partner university regarding your application.

Only after you have been appointed by Epitech, you can start the application procedures, that is to say, your nomination and application.

Unlike other Epitech students, you will have to do your own nomination (the nomination is the process during which someone proposes a student as a candidate).

Steps:

  1. Please, use this link to start the nomination process.
  2. Nominate the International Mobility Coordinator at Epitech as your nominator, between April 1 and 30, and apply for the Sandwich Program.
  3. Once the International Mobility Coordinator at Epitech has approved your nomination, you will be able to start your application.

All the documents to submit will be specified in your Shibaura user session.

Your transcripts will be directly uploaded on Shibaura's platform by the International Mobility Coordinator at Epitech, and you will need to download your Tepitech on Intra and upload it on Shibaura's portal.


To be given to Epitech campus administration:

  • Addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier

This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


2. Admission Letter

Once your application has been accepted, you will receive your acceptance letter signed by SIT.

The letter of acceptance might be required by the Japanese Immigration Office to proceed with your visa application.


3. Visa application after COE (Certificate of Eligibility) and Certificate for Completion of Registration to the ERFS System (Entrants, Returnees, Follow-up System)

In August, you will receive electronically your Certificate for Completion of Registration to ERFS system, and by post your Certificate of Eligibility.

After receiving these two required documents, you will be able to start applying for your visa.

Students who stay more than 90 days require a visa.

SIT assists by providing the necessary documents (COE - Certificate of Eligibility) for visa application.

For more information on the visa application process, click here.


Upon your arrival:

During your immigration check after the first landing in Japan, show QR codes on the Visit Japan Web screen to an officer and answer questions.

Your COE will be exchanged with a “Residence Card” upon your entry in Japan.


4. Insurance and Health

SIT covers the fee for the insurance which is university insurance for injuries or accidents related to education and research activities at SIT, called Gakkensai and Gakkenbai.

It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student. To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.

Exchange students who will stay in Japan more than 3 months must join the National Health Insurance (NHI) regardless of the kind of insurance they may already have. This is a strict legal requirement in Japan. Once you arrive in Japan, you must complete the required procedures at your local city/ward office.

For more information, you can consult the country's health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/japon

Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


Campus life

SIT has 3 campuses: Toyosu, Shibaura, and Omiya.

The campus you attend will depend on the course you register.

Please check and consider the campus location for the courses you are willing to take and the distances of each campus when you register for the courses.

Please consider distances among campuses if you wish to take courses in different campuses.

Travel times:

  • Between Shibaura and Toyosu campuses: 30 minutes
  • Between Shibaura or Toyosu and Omiya campus: 1 hour 30 minutes
accomodation:
On-campus accommodation (more information here)

SIT has an international student dormitory on the Omiya campus. This is a dormitory for International students and Japanese students. It is not only a place to live but also a community that encourages international exchanges. There are common rooms and shared kitchens on each floor. Each private room is approximately 17 square meters and is equipped with a modular bathroom with a toilet with a warm-water bidet, bed, desk and LAN access, convenience and comfort for studying and hobbies. A supervisory staff is always available to respond to needs for residents.

It is very competitive to enter the dorm, so please look for an alternative options in case you failed to stay in.


Rent: JPY 35,000/month(excluding meals and utilities), so about 200€

*One month’s rent is needed as a deposit upon entry to the dormitory

If you choose this option, please consider distances between campuses!


Off-campus accommodation (more information here)

There are several options for the housing: student dormitories, apartments, shared houses, and homestay. SIT supports entering the dormitories but even if you cannot get into a dorm due to capacity issues, SIT will introduce a private agent for looking for housing such as shared houses, apartments and homestay. Students will have a great deal of support and will have no trouble finding housing.


  • Shared house

One of the most popular housing options among the students is a “shared house”. A “shared house” is a property where the kitchen, living room, bathroom, etc. are shared with other residents.

Companies include: Frontier Co, Ltd balance plan, Borderless House, etc.


  • Apartments

If you want complete privacy, you can also sign up for an apartment on your own through a real estate agency. However, the cost will be a bit higher, and you may need to furnish the room yourself in some cases.


  • Homestay

If you want to experience the Japanese life style, a homestay may be an option for you. We will share a homestay agent’s contact information to assist you in arranging this option.
courses:
Credits

Students must take a total of 30 local credits, so 15 credits per semester to obtain 60 ECTS for the year, not counting EIP credits.


Academic Calendar

Spring semester: April to July

Fall semester: September to January


Department and courses

You will be doing what is called the Course-Taking Sandwich Program (more information here). Students have a wide range of study options from all departments and colleges. Classes are taught in English and Japanese language lessons are also available.


For Epitech students, you will have access to graduate and undergraduate Computer Science courses and Japanese language courses.

The following courses are the ones that have been approved by Epitech's pedagogical team. This list, however, only adds up to 26 local credits, this means you can take a free course each semester.


Japanese language: 2 credits (Omiya, Toyosu campus) Fall

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Embedded system (32P5): 2 credits (Omiya campus) Undergraduate level, Fall

Learn and understand the fundamentals of embedded systems. Learn and understand both hardware and software of embedded systems and their real-time constraints. Building the knowledge how to develop embedded programs using a toolkit.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Robotics (43B5): 2 credits (Toyosu campus) Undergraduate level, Spring

A robot is a system consisting of basic technologies such as mechanism, control, material, electrical and information. To apply the robot technology to the target work, it needs to design the system according to the objective. We will study how to systemize the basic technologies and how to find a solution for the social problem. In the class, we will discuss the actual problems and their solutions in the practical use of a robot to acquire the ability of solving a problem.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Introduction to Advanced Science and Technology (15M1): 2 credits (Toyosu campus) Undergraduate level, Fall

In order to become an excellent engineer or researcher, it is effective to learn about the most advanced science and technology. The scope of this course is to learn about cutting edge technologies in various research fields. This course follows an omnibus

style and is given by the teaching staff from various foreign countries. Many topics from various fields are involved such as progress in computer technology, Environmental problems, Natural disaster prevention, Advanced materials in functional or construction materials, Bio-chemistry, New Energy. The specific content of each lecture will be explained in the first class. Students will be able to study cutting-edge research in various fields and make study plans that lead to their specialized fields

in the future. You can also learn how to write basic reports.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Topics in Numerical Analysis (44V3): 2 credits (Omiya campus) Undergraduate level, Fall

Errors in numerical computation, Floating-point number, Newton’s method, contraction mapping, iterative method, simultaneous linear equation, numerical derivative, initial value problems for ordinary differential equation (ODE), Euler’s method, Runge-Kutta method.

Objectif: To be able to understand errors and error propagation in numerical computation.To be able to use several basic approaches and algorithms in numerical computation. To be able to analyze error estimation and convergence of established algorithms.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Computer Simulation 2 credits

This course introduces the fundamental and practical concepts of computer simulation as well as how to use MATLAB tool for handling and analyzing the simulation data. The topics include MATLAB programming, queue theory, etc. Assignments require an understanding of network problems and MATLAB programming.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Robot Task & System 2 credits

This lecture treats the task execution methods by the robot, and its system configuration. To achieve the desired task, advanced skills same as humans are required to the robot system. Moreover, the automatic generation ability of the task sequence according to the situation is also required. In this class, many case examples of the robot systems are introduced and explained. Understand the task execution methodology by the robot. Understand the configuration of the robot system to execute several tasks. Understand the methodology of the robot system which generates task sequence automatically, according to the situation. Acquire ability to design robot system for realizing desired task by using learned knowledge.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Human-Machine System (4567): 2 credits (Toyosu Campus) Graduate level

This course focuses on the relationship between the human and the mechanical systems. The mechanical system should have a safety and useful functionality for the human. This course includes the below topics to understand the design method of the human machine system. Topics is (1) the characteristics of the perception and the recognition, (2) design of driver assist systems, (3) the characteristics of the control action, (4) HMI (Human Machine Interface) for the mechanical system.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Advanced Computer Architecture (1511): 2 credits (Toyosu Campus) Fall

CPU chips are the most important components in computer systems and their performance has been continuing to grow. In this lecture, we study representative computer architectures that are actually used in high performance processor chips. Furthermore, through designing hardware components (i.e. function units) and simulations, we analyze and discuss how the hardware structure influences the performance. The material to read is provided in pdf at Scomb and Reading Assignments are directed in advance. To help understanding in reading, several basic questions are also provided about the contents of the pre-directed reading material. At every class, students are divided into groups and discuss what he/she understood through the reading material and his/her answer to the questions. Discussion is made in each breakout room of Zoom. Then, students give presentations in group order. The instructor checks the presentations and gives lecture/comments to make up for missing content in their presentation.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Management of Innovation: 2 credits (Toyosu Campus) Graduate Level, Fall

This course will start from providing basic understanding of innovation from view points of history of society, economics, technology and corporate management. Then participants will obtain practical knowledge of innovation to apply for business cases to develop business strategy by understanding real examples. This course will discuss innovation with global view point. After the guidance and introduction of innovation concept in the first lecture, participants are requested to chose own innovation topic to study. In each ecture participants need to prepare short presentation according to the subject provided in the previous lecture. Discussion after each presentation participants obtain deeper understanding of innovation aspects with real examples

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Advanced Robotic Manipulation: 2 credits (Shibaura Campus) Graduate level, Fall

This lecture gives advancesd mathematical introduction to robotics. Robotic engineering consistes of basic theory and practice. The basic theory begins with mathematical definition related to position, orientation, and coordinate frames. Furthermore, they are led to robot's rotation, transformation, and control technologies. Meanwhile, the practics includes mechanism, motor drives, electrical hardware, and software design. They assist mutually and the both are indispensable. The former theory has been evolved

and changed gradually. Therefore, if students who want to master advanced robotics, they need to learn the advanced theory.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Embedded Systems Engineering: 2 credits (Omiya Campus) Graduate level, Fall

The main purpose of this class is to understand and execute systems engineering in embedded system and M2M(Machine to Machine) system. Requirement analysis, modeling, system architecture design, and project management in embedded system and M2M system are introduced and discussed.The purpose of this class is to understand and execute systems engineering in embedded system, IoT(Internet of Things), and M2M(Machine to Machine) system. To understand technology, requirement, and architecture of embedded system. To understand life cycle of embedded system, requirement analysis, architecture design To understand system architecture and networks for M2M system.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Bionic and biomimetic system engineering: 2 credits

The purpose of this course is to learn basics of biology and physiology, measuring biological signals, signal processing, information processing, system integration, biomimetic technologies, and ethics. Through learning the topics, students acquire wide view required for developing biomedical systems.


Important notes

  • Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits).
  • The courses are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.
  • The course list is given for information only. It can change from year to year.
  • If a course is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.
  • Any Tech 4 abroad involves an EIP! Take advantage of the free slots you will have to advance it.
cost:
Financial overview (4th yeat at Epitech)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the tuition fees at the partner university.
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.).


Other expenses

  • Roundtrip flights: from 800€
  • Visa: 18€
  • Additional insurance: 300-600€ depending on the coverage (same as above)
  • Deposit for room if you live in the dormitory
  • Registration fee at SIT: 170€ (30 000 yen)


Estimated monthly budget

The local currency is the Japanese yen. 1 € = 176¥ (rate in October 2025).

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.

When coming to Japan, you should estimate that you will be spending every month between 1000€ to 1500€.


  • Housing & utilities

250 to 500€ + 40€ of utilities. The price of an apartment in the city center is approximately the same as a mid-size city in France.


As SIT has two campuses located one hour and half from each other, with one located in inner Tokyo (Toyosu) and the other on the outskirts of the capital (Higashi-Omiya), prices can be very different.The closer you try living to the Toyosu campus, the more rent will be expensive, while the rent near Higashi-Omiya is more affordable. This marks a problem as most of the classes about computer science are in Toyosu with the Omiya campus offering close to none. You should therefore try choosing with care where you decide to live.

Rent in cities close to the Toyosu campus: 500€ - 800€

Rent in cities close to the Omiya campus: 350€ - 600€


  • Food & eating out ~150-300€

Around 6 euros for a meal in a basic restaurant

Around 15 euros for a meal in a mid-range restaurant

The price of basic food is about the same as in France (Paris), except for imported products which will be more expensive and local products which will be cheaper.


  • Transportation ~100€

Expect to pay anything between 100€ to 300€ depending on how much you travel in a month.


The distance between the Omiya campus and the Toyosu campus is one hour and a half. There is no direct train line to join the two. It will cost about 7.50€ to go from one campus to the other, so a 15€ round trip. While it will be rare to have to do the trip every day of the week, expect to do it at least twice. Depending on where you live in Tokyo, you will pay at least 100€ a month for travelling.

You can get a commuter pass which will reduce the price of transportation; however, this pass is only applicable to one route and that route only, back and forth.

To take the example of the trip from the Omiya campus to the Toyosu campus:

  • Start from the Higashi-Omiya station > Get down at the Ikebukuro Station > Take the metro from Ikebukuro station > Get down at the Toyosu station


Same trip backwards to go from the Toyosu campus to the Omiya campus.

You will pay only once when you get the commuter pass (about 90€ for one month), and won’t pay anything more when travelling between those stations.

You can get down at any stop on that line between Higashi-Omiya and Ikebukuro, and Ikebukuro and Toyosu, but you will pay extra cost if you get out of a station after those. For example, if you go to the station after the Ikebukuro station, you will pay the normal fare between those two stations. You can get a student discount for the shikansen via a machine in the university.


  • Health insurance ~12€
  • Phone, internet ~20-50€

We recommend you to make a mobile contract at one of discount mobile phone companies in Japan, for example: "Rakuten Mobile", "UQ mobile" provided by KDDI, "Y!mobile" by SoftBank, and Sakura Mobile. With a new SIM card, you can use your own smart phone in Japan. A previous student has recommended Rakuten for the phone plan because it is the cheapest for a good amount of data.


  • Leisure ~80-150€


The prices are indicative and may vary.


Additional information (specifics, advice, useful links, etc.)

Students can find the government-approved information site for studying in Japan operated by the Japan Student Services Organization through the link here.

Please note that you can work within a limit of 28 hours per week. The university can help you with your job search, however, it is important to note that it will not be in the IT field.
